question: Find the H.C.F. of 18, 54, and 72 is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the smallest number in the set: 18.

Check if 18 divides the other numbers: 54 ÷ 18 = 3 and 72 ÷ 18 = 4.

Since 18 is a factor of both 54 and 72, it is the Highest Common Factor.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given numbers: 18, 54, 72

Method: Prime Factorization

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/144a94c1cfb0bb93274019fdcd42e5e0f6874f970b191131294465d4f75131cf.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2¹ × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 54 = 2¹ × 3³

⇒ Prime factorization of 72 = 2³ × 3²

⇒ HCF = Product of common prime factors with the lowest power

⇒ HCF = 2¹ × 3²

⇒ HCF = 2 × 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is 1.

Methods to find HCF

HCF can be found using Prime Factorization, the Listing Factors method, or the Long Division (Euclidean) method.
